title: "Conformance status"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

*Last updated: 2026-11-12 (development round 9).*

sasonr only accepts a feature once its test cases reproduce the output of
**real SAS 9.4** (TS1M7, Linux). Expected results are never taken from
documentation examples, book printouts, other interpreters or hand
derivation: in early experiments each of these was wrong at least once.

## How results are compared

Every test program is run in a fresh SAS session and in sasonr. Four layers
are compared:

| Layer | What is compared |
|---|---|
| **L-DS** | Every WORK data set at the end of the program: data set names, row count, column names and order, every cell (numbers bit for bit, no tolerance; character values without trailing blanks) |
| **L-ATTR** | Variable type, length, format, informat and label |
| **L-LOG** | Key log diagnostics in order (`NOTE: The data set ... has N observations`, missing-value notes, uninitialized variables, unresolved macro references, ...) |
| **L-LST** | Listing output, line by line in order (whitespace normalised) |

Own test programs also compare the PUT output and the files a program
writes. Two kinds of failure are tracked first in every round because they are
*silent*: an L-DS mismatch (wrong result) and a program on which SAS stops
with an ERROR but sasonr keeps running (too lenient). Unsupported features
are not failures: sasonr stops with a `sasonr_unsupported` condition.

## Test suite 1: single-feature corpus (1,965 programs)

The programs come from the test corpus of the open-source OpenSAS
interpreter (Apache-2.0, invented data). SAS ran 1,680 of them normally and
stopped with an error on 285.

### Current status

| | Programs |
|---|---|
| SAS ran normally | 1,680 |
| sasonr ran to completion | **1,015** |
| sasonr stopped: feature not supported yet | 648 |
| sasonr stopped: error | 17 |
| **All layers identical to SAS** | **988** (97.3% of completed) |
| L-DS mismatches | **0** |
| SAS stopped with an error but sasonr kept running | **0** of 285 |
| SAS stopped with an error: sasonr reports a SAS ERROR at the same step / fails loud / R error | 43 / 225 / 17 |

## Test suite 2: function-by-function tests

The feature inventory is exported from SAS itself (`sashelp.vfunc`,
`dictionary.formats`): 1,096 functions (409 in Base SAS) and 1,032
formats/informats. Each function gets 20–60 cases covering documented
examples, missing and special missing values, numeric and character
boundaries, argument counts and types, result length and `_ERROR_`.

| Stage | Status |
|---|---|
| Pilot: SUBSTR, SCAN, COMPRESS, INDEX, CATX, ROUND, INPUT, PUT, INTNX, INTCK | **343 / 370 identical to SAS**, 27 fail loud |
| Verification matrix and random probes: 188 functions, 5,322 matrix cases | 110 verified, 43 partial, 29 approximate, 2 differ (CONSTANT, MDY; fail loud), 4 clock-dependent |
| Verification matrix: 144 formats and informats, 1,746 cases | 94 verified, 13 partial, 37 without cases yet |

Every case is compared exactly: value bit for bit, type, length,
`_ERROR_`, the log NOTEs of its step and its PUT output. Each function or
format is one SAS program with one step per case. With strict mode (the
default) the 28 approximate functions stop with `sasonr_not_verified`;
measured with `sasonr.strict = FALSE`, 718 of their 1,077 cases are
bit-identical and 266 differ in the last bits.

## Test suite 3: end-to-end programs from books

End-to-end example programs from published SAS textbooks, used as an
internal acceptance suite. Only our own index and the SAS-produced results
are used; no program text or output from the books is published.

| Group | Programs | Run by SAS | sasonr: all layers | not supported yet | wrong results |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Introductory SAS programming examples | 136 | 120 | **47** | 71 | 0 |
| Clinical (pharmaceutical) programming examples | 65 | 34 | **13** | 21 | 0 |

The clinical programs are mainly blocked by ODS statements (12) and `OPTIONS MISSING=` (4).

## Test suite 4: SAS rounding

About 21,000 rounding points generated on SAS 9.4 (ROUND, ROUNDE, ROUNDZ,
INT/FLOOR/CEIL, `w.d`, BEST, Z, COMMA, DOLLAR, PERCENT, E formats) plus PROC
display programs. Inputs are exact IEEE-754 bit patterns.

| Group | Before round 7a | After round 7a |
|---|---|---|
| ROUND | 95.6% | **98.5%** |
| ROUNDE, ROUNDZ, INT, FLOOR, CEIL, ... | 95.9% | **99.6%** |
| Formats | 87.8% | **96.2%** |

The remaining points (edge windows of the ROUND fuzz, half-way edges of
formats, very narrow BEST widths, PROC MEANS default decimals for very large
or very small values) stop with `sasonr_unsupported`; none returns a
different value silently. Target: 100%.

## Offline conformance cases

From round 7a all cases are stored as offline fixtures (program, invented
data, SAS output with data sets as `.sas7bdat`), so regression runs without
SAS:

| Layer | Cases |
|---|---|
| Our own cases (parser, functions, FREQ statistics, rounding, semantics, function and format matrices, function probes, procedure statistic probes, error handling) | 7,854 |
| Single-feature corpus and book programs | 2,119 |

Round 12.1 (review of round 12): 7,550 of 9,975 cases bit-identical, 2,363
fail loud, no data set value differs silently. The two new probes (nearly
constant data for PROC MEANS, symmetric argument lists for DATA step
SKEWNESS) fail loud as whole programs but fixed the rules for nearly
constant data, the STD cut-off and negative CSS; the moment kernel now fails
loud on any overflow, underflow or NaN instead of returning a missing value.

Round 12 (PROC MEANS moment statistics): 7,550 of 9,973 cases
bit-identical, 2,361 fail loud, no data set value differs silently and no
program on which SAS stops with an ERROR runs in sasonr. The CSS family of
PROC MEANS / SUMMARY (CSS, USS, VAR, STD, STDERR, CV, T, KURTOSIS) is
bit-identical to SAS on four new probes (more than 3,000 values per
statistic, with FREQ, WEIGHT and VARDEF=), so 31 programs that stopped in
strict mode now agree with SAS in every layer.

Round 11 (verification integrity): 7,452 of 9,969 cases bit-identical,
2,455 fail loud, no data set value differs silently and no program on which
SAS stops with an ERROR runs in sasonr. The count is lower than in round 10
because the rules are stricter: a case passes only when every layer agrees
(a display or log difference alone is a difference), a fail loud or R error
where SAS stops with an ERROR is no longer counted as agreement, functions
are gated by the context of the call (WHERE expressions have no cases yet),
and BEST32. values whose rounding SAS does not decide consistently fail loud.

Round 10: 7,891 of 9,968 cases bit-identical (including programs on which
SAS and sasonr both stop with an ERROR; for the new error-handling cases the
data sets SAS leaves behind and the log are compared too), 2,015 fail loud,
**no data set value differs silently** and no program on which SAS stops with
an ERROR runs in sasonr. Procedure statistics are now verified per statistic
(see the feature registry): sums, means, counts, minima, maxima and quantiles
of PROC MEANS and PROC SQL are bit-identical to SAS; PROC MEANS standard
deviations and the statistics derived from them are not yet and stop the
program in strict mode.

## Known gaps

- PROC MEANS `SKEWNESS`, `PRT` and the confidence limits are approximate
  (SKEWNESS about 97 % of probe values; PRT and CLM need SAS's t
  distribution); `CSS`, `USS`, `VAR`, `STD`, `STDERR`, `CV`, `T` and
  `KURTOSIS` are bit-identical since round 12. PROC SQL `STDERR`/`CV` are
  approximate. In strict mode approximate statistics stop the program.
- `EXP`, `LOG10`, `COSH`, `TANH`, `PERM` and the probability functions
  differ from SAS in the last bits for some arguments.
- After an execution-time ERROR in a DATA step the partly written data sets
  are not reproduced yet (fail loud).

- Function examples: 698 SAS-verified calls were generated for the reference
  pages; **15 calls return a different value from SAS** (CAT, CATT, COUNTC,
  FINV, JULDATE, LOGSDF, PUTC, QUOTE, STRIP, SYMGET, TRANWRD, TRIMN, YRDIF)
  and 2 are rejected (INDEXC with several excerpts). They are excluded from
  the examples and are the first items to fix.

- PROC FREQ: CHISQ, FISHER and EXACT FISHER are verified (whole SAS cases
  agree in every layer, the listing line for line); BINOMIAL, CMH and the
  other statistics are not verified and stop the program in strict mode,
  through the same PROC statistics registry as every other procedure.
- ODS output (HTML/RTF) is not compared yet.
- No statistical procedures beyond MEANS/FREQ yet.
